goal: Removes the Boost.Test dependency and replaces it with a project-specific unit test framework
Aims to unify inconsistent assertion styles and remove a dependency with bugs and abandonment risk
reviewability: Ready to review: author fixed every substantive bug found within about two weeks, CI passing and mergeable
Expect further iteration on details like CHECK_NO_DISPLAY follow-ups but no blocker to reviewing now
agreement: Strong concept ACK citing repository-specific context and extensibility (josibake)
Concept ACK paired with concrete bugs found in review, all fixed by the author (jeanpablojp)
Design questions on static_assert vs compile error and keeping && / || worked through to agreed design (maflcko)
No standing objection to the change's direction remains

categories.name: build
why: P3 because dropping Boost.Test from depends, cmake, and vcpkg is a modest simplification with no urgency
One build regression was flagged, removing a fatal-warnings flag too broadly, and was restored
Benefit is a cleanup, not a fix to an active breakage

categories.name: tests
why: P2 because it changes how every contributor writes and debugs unit tests across the whole suite
Removes dependency risk and unifies macros that currently exist in three or four incompatible forms
Review surfaced real correctness risk in the new framework itself, a segfault, missing flush, and broken seed reproducibility, all fixed during review
